results.text: Combined dapagliflozin and pioglitazone therapy in diabetic nephropathy: no added benefit beyond monotherapy in inflammation and fibrosis. Effect of pioglitazone on urinary liver-type fatty acid-binding protein concentrations in diabetes patients with microalbuminuria. Urinary liver-type fatty acid-binding protein (L-FABP) is a useful marker for renal tubulointerstitial injury. Pioglitazone is reported to be effective in early diabetic nephropathy. The aim of the present study was to determine whether pioglitazone affects urinary L-FABP levels in diabetic nephropathy patients with microalbuminuria.

Pioglitazone improves tamoxifen-induced renal injury in rat model through modulating oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis signaling. One prevalent chemotherapeutic medication used to treat breast cancer is tamoxifen (TAM), and several off-label uses. However, when used as an antineoplastic drug in clinical settings, it causes harmful cellular effects such as renal damage.
